role_agent_name: Induced seismicity and geophysical monitoring lead (GEOP)
abstract: Maintains seismic monitoring network deployment logs and baseline microseismic event tracking records
system_message:
You are the Induced seismicity and geophysical monitoring lead (GEOP). Your business responsibilities include maintaining seismic monitoring network deployment logs, tracking baseline microseismic event records, and documenting magnetotelluric sounding survey results across exploratory geothermal prospects.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains seismic monitoring network deployment logs and baseline microseismic event tracking records（SEIS）
information_points.content:
GEOP-SEIS-9CM：For the Tauhara Extension Step-Out Drilling, live telemetry confirms that the seismic monitoring array is active within a 10 km radius, while the prospect has accumulated a continuous baseline seismic monitoring duration of 75 d of uninterrupted background microseismicity recording.
GEOP-SEIS-K2M：For the Rotokawa North Deep Fracture Probe, operational confirmation verifies that the seismic monitoring array is active across the permanent surface and borehole network within a 10 km radius, and baseline records show a continuous baseline seismic monitoring duration of 90 d prior to spud date.
GEOP-SEIS-ZYM：For the Ngatamariki Peripheral Thermal Campaign, the permanent seismic monitoring array is active with confirmed live telemetry within a 10 km radius, and the local pre-drilling surveillance record establishes a continuous baseline seismic monitoring duration of 120 d.

information_points.title: Magnetotelluric sounding survey（MTEL）
information_points.content:
GEOP-MTEL-ZL4：For the Tauhara Extension Step-Out Drilling, magnetotelluric sounding data identify the clay cap resistivity depth boundary at 600 m depth within the campaign target exploratory sector.
GEOP-MTEL-I4B：According to the 3D inversion survey for the Ngatamariki Peripheral Thermal Campaign, the clay cap resistivity depth boundary extends to a depth of 450 m.
GEOP-MTEL-G2U：Magnetotelluric 3D inversion survey results for the Rotokawa North Deep Fracture Probe delineate the clay cap resistivity depth boundary at 750 m from the surface to the base of the conductive smectite cap.
